# kemp_match_rule (Resource)

Manages a content matching rule. Attach it to a real server or SubVS (match_rules) for content switching, or to a virtual service's pre_process_rules to set flags for later rules.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Route /api/ requests to a dedicated SubVS (see match_rules on
# kemp_sub_virtual_service).
resource "kemp_match_rule" "api" {
  name       = "api_path"
  pattern    = "/api/"
  match_type = "prefix"
}

# Match on a header instead of the URL, and set a flag other rules can check.
resource "kemp_match_rule" "mobile" {
  name             = "mobile_clients"
  header           = "User-Agent"
  pattern          = "(iPhone|Android)"
  case_insensitive = true
  set_flag         = 1
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Rule name: letters, digits and underscores. Changing this forces a new rule.
- `pattern` (String) Pattern to match against the request URL, or against the header named by header.

### Optional

- `case_insensitive` (Boolean) Match without regard to case.
- `fail_on_match` (Boolean) Reject the connection when the rule matches.
- `header` (String) Request header to match instead of the URL. Empty (the default) matches the URL.
- `include_host` (Boolean) Prepend the Host header to the URL before matching.
- `include_query` (Boolean) Include the query string in the URL being matched.
- `match_type` (String) How pattern is matched: regex, prefix or postfix. Defaults to regex.
- `negate` (Boolean) Invert the match: the rule matches when pattern does not.
- `only_if_flag` (Number) Only evaluate this rule if this flag is set. Flags are 1-9.
- `only_if_not_flag` (Number) Only evaluate this rule if this flag is not set. Flags are 1-9.
- `set_flag` (Number) Flag to set when the rule matches, for later rules to check. Flags are 1-9.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The rule name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Rules are imported by name.
terraform import kemp_match_rule.example my_rule_name
```
